newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia strike snarls export of 90,000 bags coffee.
newsitem.headline: Colombia strike snarls export of 90,000 bags coffee.

text.p: A strike by Colombian dock workers at the main Pacific coast port of Buenaventura has halted the loading of 90,000 60-kg bags of coffee destined for export, a National Coffee Growers' Federation chief said Wednesday.

The dock strike was declared late Tuesday and began to bite Wednesday. About 60 percent of Colombia's coffee exports are shipped from Buenaventura and Federation commercial manager John Naranjo said 180 trucks, transporting 500 bags each, were currently caught in the action.

"This strike is very worrisome. The port of Buenaventura is totally immobilized. According to our figures there are 180 trucks caught in the strike each one with 500 (60-kg) bags," Naranjo told Reuters.
He said the federation was at the moment waiting to see the outcome of talks between striking dockers and port authorities, ship owners and cargo operators. Talks were scheduled for later Wednesday.

Naranjo declined to speculate on the duration of the strike but said it would not be easy to simply divert loads destined for export to the Caribbean coast ports, which currently handle about 40 percent of Colombia's exports.
